official_answers.text: A holiday to celebrate U.S. independence (from Britain)

why_it_matters.text: July 4 (Independence Day, 'the Fourth of July') celebrates the day the Continental Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence in 1776 — formally breaking from Britain. Americans celebrate with fireworks, parades, BBQs, and family gatherings. It became an official federal holiday in 1870. America's 250th birthday is coming up in 2026.

fun_fact.text: On July 2, 1776, the Continental Congress voted yes for independence. John Adams wrote his wife Abigail: this day will be celebrated forever with 'Pomp and Parade... Bells, Bonfires and Illuminations.' He was right about everything except the date. Congress finalized the Declaration's wording on July 4 — and that's the day America remembered.
